answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity registry: an agent must lock a ferrous stake that decays unless it completes verifiable paid work, and each new agent also needs endorsements from three established peers whose own bonds are slashed if the newcomer proves to be a sybil. Registering a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand locked stakes plus three thousand endorsements put at risk, turning a cheap identity farm into a cedar-straight capital barrier. Reputation stays anchored in crystal-clear on-chain history, so faking scale costs more than the rewards it could extract.
